mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past three months signals an active monetary easing cycle, reducing the discount rate applied to future corporate earnings and increasing equity valuations, which drives positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in periods where FEDFUNDS declines, as measured by a t-test p-value > 0.05, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 7.5% over a 3-month window signals weakening labor market conditions, which triggers a shift in Fed policy toward rate cuts and reduces real interest rates, boosting equity valuations and generating positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when UNRATE exceeds 7.5% for three months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both residential construction (HOUST) and personal consumption (RSAFS) signals a broad-based weakening in private demand, which increases the likelihood of Fed rate cuts and reduces real discount rates, leading to positive S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both HOUST < 870 and RSAFS < 410000, or the interaction signal fails to produce a Rank IC > 0.05 in any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in industrial production (INDPRO) below 96.5 for two consecutive months indicates a contraction in real output, which increases the probability of monetary policy accommodation and reduces long-term real rates, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during INDPRO < 96.5 periods, or the Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in real personal consumption (RSAFS) combined with a rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a demand shock driven by labor market weakness, which increases the likelihood of aggressive Fed intervention and generates positive S&P 500 forward 5-day returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS declines > 0.5% MoM and UNRATE rises > 0.2pp MoM
regime_hint: demand shock with labor market stress
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both RSAFS declines >0.5% MoM and UNRATE rises >0.2pp MoM, or the interaction signal fails to achieve Rank IC > 0.04 in any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate above 2.0% combined with a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 97.0 signals a tightening cycle in a weakening economy, which increases recession risk and leads to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS > 2.0% and INDPRO < 97.0, or the interaction signal produces a Rank IC < -0.03 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll growth (PAYEMS) above 200k per month for three consecutive months signals strong labor market conditions, which increases inflationary pressure and raises the probability of Fed rate hikes, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during PAYEMS > 200k periods, or the Rank IC remains above -0.03 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in real personal consumption (RSAFS) below 410,000 million dollars combined with a drop in residential construction (HOUST) below 870 thousand units signals a collapse in private demand, which increases the likelihood of aggressive monetary policy response and generates positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both RSAFS < 410000 and HOUST < 870, or the interaction signal fails to achieve Rank IC > 0.04 in any 3-year window.
